subject: Throughput & latency playbook — follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Nguyen <elliot@lightningcart.com>, Kara Simms <kara@lightningcart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Throughput & latency playbook — follow-up and next steps

Hi Elliot / Kara,

Thanks again for the call this morning — appreciated the clear prioritization. Quick recap and recommended next steps so we have alignment before the pilot: 

Recap of signals you shared:
- 95th percentile latency target: ~80ms for user-facing endpoints (30–50ms ideal for some pages).
- Typical steady QPS: 300–500; expected peak bursts up to ~1,200 concurrent requests for 10–30 minute windows during flash sales.
- Model: GPT-like LLM for short-response completions (~120 tokens on average).
- Compliance: VPC-only for production (we heard you want to evaluate hosted first, but production requires VPC).

Initial recommendation (pilot path):
1) Short hosted pilot (2 weeks) to gather real traffic profiling and tail-latency characteristics. This lets us validate batching behavior and prefix cache benefits quickly.
2) If p95 tail latency or sustained QPS patterns exceed the breakeven point (we typically see Dedicated become cost-effective & predictable when sustained QPS > ~800 with tight p95 SLOs), we propose a Dedicated reserved-capacity trial.
3) Parallel security check: we will start the VPC intake checklist so we understand the work required for an eventual private deployment; no blocker to starting hosted pilot.

Requests / next steps for your team:
- Share a short sample traffic trace (one CSV with timestamped request sizes and average tokens) and any SLO windows you must enforce.
- Confirm availability for a 30–45 minute kickoff next Tuesday (10/03 or 10/04 window we suggested) so Ben can run a quick benchmark and agree on instrumentation points.

Attached: playbook-diff.xlsx (pilot checklist) and a lightweight bench spec we use internally.

Goal: run hosted pilot -> observe real p95 and queueing -> decide (hosted vs Dedicated) based on observed p95 and sustained QPS profile.

Thanks,
Jordan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
phone: (415) 555-0132

---

From: Elliot Nguyen <elliot@lightningcart.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Kara Simms <kara@lightningcart.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput & latency playbook — follow-up and next steps

Jordan — thanks for the tidy recap. A couple quick clarifications: 

1) On the bursts: when we say 1,200 concurrent requests, that’s concurrent HTTP POSTs hitting the generation endpoint; average token count ~120 but some requests hit 300–400 tokens during longer responses. Bursts are usually 15–25 minutes.
2) For SLOs: we need p95 <100ms for core checkout flows and p95 <200ms is tolerable for non-critical pages.
3) Pilot timing: next week looks good. Can you confirm whether the hosted pilot supports a traffic replay mode so we can feed sampled traffic rather than live traffic? We prefer a replay to mitigate user impact.

We’ll pull a sample trace and share it by end of day tomorrow.

—Elliot
Head of Engineering | LightningCart
elliot@lightningcart.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Nguyen <elliot@lightningcart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput & latency playbook — follow-up and next steps

Appreciate the quick reply, Elliot. Answering your two points and adding a few specifics so we can lock the kickoff: 

1) Replay mode: yes — we support a traffic replay for the hosted pilot. We accept sampled request payloads and can run them against an isolated pilot cluster to measure queuing, batching efficiency, and tail behaviour. We’ll need sanitized logs (no PII) and timestamps.

2) Burst characterization: given your burst length (15–25m) and token variability, our initial hypothesis is:
- If p95 at your sampled replay is <= 120ms on hosted with observed peak QPS ~1,200, you can likely keep production on Hosted with autoscaling and prefix caching tuned.
- If p95 > 120ms and you see sustained 800+ QPS slices, Dedicated will provide lower and more consistent tail latency due to reserved pools and harder isolation.

Bench & instrumentation we’ll run:
- End-to-end p50/p95/p99, service queue lengths, GPU utilization, batch size distribution, and token throughput.
- We’ll also run a model-variant sensitivity test (float16 vs q4/q8 quant) to see cost vs latency trade-offs.

Proposed checklist items for pilot kickoff (30–45m):
- LightningCart to share a sanitized replay bundle (CSV + sample payloads) + SLO windows.
- Redwood to provision an isolated hosted pilot cluster and run baseline replay (24–48h) and share results.
- If results indicate Dedicated needed, we will prepare a Dedicated trial quote and capacity sketch.

Ben is copied to scope the bench tasks. Are you available Tue Oct 3 at 10:00am PT? If not, Wed Oct 4 at 11:00am PT works for us.

Thanks,
Jordan

Quick technical addendum from Ben: 

Elliot — echoing Jordan and adding a few bench specifics to make the replay results actionable: 
- Please include request/response sizes (bytes) and token counts per request in the replay bundle.
- Include a 10-minute sample from a flash sale window if possible — that will reveal batching/shim behavior.
- We'll run three model-variant passes: full precision, q8, and q4 to map latency vs cost. Attaching a short bench spec (latency-bench-2026.pdf) that shows the metrics we’ll produce.

If hosted pilot shows p95 under 120ms at your peak replay, we’ll recommend staying on Hosted for faster time-to-market and lower ops burden. If p95 remains above target and you need consistent sub-100ms p95, we’ll draft a Dedicated capacity sketch (reservations per GPU type + estimated monthly cost) and map the migration checklist.

I’ll be on the kickoff to run the replay; Jordan — if you confirm Tue 10/03 10:00am PT we’ll lock it.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
